pool.text: Although now in Poland, it had been traditionally a part of Bohemia until this year.
Hitler ordered the German Army to enter Prague and proclaimed Bohemia and Moravia a German protectorate.
Prague witnessed the assassination of Reinhard Heydrich during Operation Anthropoid by Czechoslovak heroes.
Prague suffered several bombing raids by the US Army Air Forces in February.
An uprising against Germany occurred on 5 May, two days before Germany capitulated.
The world's largest Stalin Monument was unveiled on Letná hill.
The world's largest Stalin Monument on Letná hill was destroyed.
Students demonstrated at Strahov on 31 October.
The 4th Czechoslovak Writers' Congress took a strong position against the regime.
The Soviet Union led Warsaw Pact countries to invade Czechoslovakia and Prague.
Jan Palach and Jan Zajíc committed suicide by self-immolation in January and February.
The Velvet Revolution crowded the streets of Prague after riot police beat back a student demonstration.
The stadium hosted Spartakiads during the communist era until this year.
The military occupation of Czechoslovakia by the Red Army finally ended.
The Historic Centre of Prague and its monuments were inscribed as a cultural UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Prague became the capital city of the new Czech Republic after the Velvet Divorce.
The IMF and World Bank summits took place in Prague alongside anti-globalisation riots.
Prague suffered from widespread floods that damaged buildings and its underground transport system.
The O2 Arena hosted the IIHF World Championship in this year.
The Allegro restaurant received the first Michelin star in the post-Communist part of Central Europe.
